name: Convertly Media Optimizer
author: Riandre van der Voorden

sections.description:
Large media files can make WordPress pages slow and consume unnecessary storage. Convertly Media Optimizer helps you reduce file sizes, create modern image formats, and manage optimization from the WordPress dashboard.

The processing happens through Convertly, so your WordPress server does not have to perform the heavy conversion work.

Optimize your Media Library in minutes

  • Optimize every new upload automatically. Keep your normal WordPress publishing workflow.
  • Bulk optimize existing media. Improve files already in your Media Library with a few clicks.
  • Create WebP and AVIF images. Serve modern formats supported by today’s browsers.
  • Resize oversized images. Avoid serving originals that are much larger than your site needs.
  • Protect your originals. Keep local backups and restore them when needed.
  • Use an optional Image CDN. Deliver optimized images and responsive sizes without uploading your library again.
  • Make common media edits. Remove backgrounds, convert formats, create thumbnails, add watermarks, clean metadata, and more.
  • Bring in Convertly Storage files. Browse and import approved workspace media without leaving WordPress.

Built for everyday WordPress work

Convertly works in the background after you upload a file. You can follow optimization progress from WordPress and continue working while larger jobs are processed.

The Image CDN and Convertly Storage features are optional. Enable only the features your site needs under Settings > Convertly Media.

More than a basic image compressor

Convertly combines several media workflows that normally require separate plugins. In addition to image compression, it can process selected video and audio files, restore backed-up originals, run on-demand media tools, import files from site-isolated Convertly Storage, and deliver existing WordPress images through an origin-fetch CDN without re-uploading the Media Library.

This is the official WordPress plugin for the Convertly service. It is published and maintained by Convertly.

What you need

You need a Convertly account and a WordPress site token. Each site receives its own token, so agencies can keep client sites and their media separate.

Create an account or learn more at https://convertly.sh.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP in Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Convertly Media Optimizer.
  3. Open Settings > Convertly Media.
  4. Paste the WordPress site token created for this site.
  5. Choose how you want new uploads and existing media to be optimized.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Convertly account?

Yes. The plugin uses Convertly to process media and requires a WordPress site token. Use one WordPress site token per client install and choose No storage or Isolated storage when you create it. This keeps each client’s media access separate.

Is this the official Convertly plugin?

Yes. Convertly Media Optimizer is published and maintained by the owner of the Convertly service and the convertly.sh domain.

Does optimization happen on my WordPress server?

No. Convertly performs the heavy media processing, helping reduce the CPU and memory work required from your WordPress hosting.

Can I import assets from Convertly Storage?

Yes, when storage access is enabled for the site’s token. Open Media > Convertly Storage to browse and import files. Convertly remembers imported files so it can avoid creating unnecessary duplicates. If the token has No storage, optimization still works.

Can Convertly Storage auto-import into WordPress?

Yes. Enable auto-import under Settings > Convertly Media when the plugin uses a WordPress site token that has isolated storage enabled. The plugin periodically adds new workspace files to the Media Library and skips files it has already imported.

How do I enable Image CDN mode?

First create your delivery setup in Convertly. Then open Settings > Convertly Media > Image CDN in WordPress and use the automatic setup button. The built-in test shows a real optimized image before you enable delivery.

When enabled, eligible Media Library images are delivered through Convertly and cached for faster repeat visits. Your original images remain in WordPress and are not copied into Convertly Storage.

Does this plugin connect to an external service?

Yes. Convertly is the service that processes and returns your media. This connection is required for optimization, conversion, and storage-import features.

  • Service: Convertly (https://convertly.sh)
  • Privacy Policy: https://convertly.sh/privacy
  • Terms of Service: https://convertly.sh/terms

When you use this plugin, your WordPress site sends the media files and related file information needed to complete the action you selected. The plugin does not send visitor analytics or tracking data to Convertly.
sections.changelog:
0.7.18

  • Fixed: The Image CDN preview detects a deleted or renamed delivery namespace, refreshes the active public namespace list, saves the repaired namespace, and retries automatically.

0.7.17

  • Fixed: The first-run welcome modal now removes ThickBox content padding, keeps the banner flush, and pins actions to the footer.

0.7.16

  • Improved: Image CDN settings now live behind a top-level settings tab separate from upload optimization.
  • Improved: The first-run welcome modal uses a stronger Convertly banner and keeps all actions in a modal footer.

0.7.15

  • Improved: Settings now clearly separate upload optimization from Image CDN delivery, with local WebP/AVIF described as a non-CDN fallback.
  • Fixed: The first-run welcome guide now falls back to a native modal if WordPress ThickBox opens only the overlay.

0.7.14

  • Improved: Automatic optimization choices now use clearly separated, responsive WordPress-style option fields.

0.7.13

  • Improved: Convertly optimization details in the Media Library now use native wp-admin icons and metadata styling.

0.7.12

  • New: Image CDN delivery quality supports Eco, Balanced, Best, and fixed custom modes.
  • Improved: Existing installations retain their fixed CDN quality while new installations default to adaptive Balanced delivery.

0.7.11

  • Fixed: WordPress image rewrites and CDN setup previews now use cdn.convertly.sh instead of the Convertly API hostname.

0.7.10

  • Fixed: Image CDN setup and test feedback now appears beside the Image CDN controls instead of at the top of the page.
  • Changed: WordPress no longer creates delivery namespaces or signing keys; those resources are managed in Convertly.
  • Improved: Automatic setup selects the existing default public namespace and the pencil editor lists other existing public namespaces.

Earlier release notes are included in changelog.txt inside the plugin package.
